We find that large-scale stable magnetic fields can extract angular momentum efficiently from the star via coupling to stellar winds, producing slowly rotating single hot subdwarfs and thus providing a possible explanation to both the long rotation periods provided by asteroseismology and low spectroscopic rotational velocities. This hints magnetic braking could be an important component of the rotational properties of low-mass stellar mergers.

entries.title: Constraint on particle mass of dark matter based on XTE J1814-338 observation and DANS model
entries.abstract: The small observed radius of neutron star XTE J1814-338 (with mass of $1.21_{-0.05}^{+0.05}$ $M_{\odot}$ and radius of $7_{-0.4}^{+0.4}$ $\rm{km}$) poses a great challenge to the traditional neutron star model composed of normal nuclear matter. The dark matter admixed neutron star (DANS) model provides a clue to solve this challenge. By employing the self-interacting fermionic dark matter model, we investigate the effects of dark matter parameters including the particle mass, self-interaction strength, and mass fraction of dark matter on the properties of DANSs. Our results indicate that the joint constraints from the observation of XTE J1814-338 and the astrophysical limits on the dark matter self-interaction cross section derived from observations of different colliding galaxy clusters can provide effective constraints on the particle mass of dark matter. Specifically, to simultaneously satisfy the small radius of XTE J1814-338 and the self-interaction limit, the particle mass of self-interacting fermionic dark matter is constrained to the range from sub-GeV to a few GeV.

entries.title: Microcaustics: Fast GPU-Accelerated Dynamical Microlensing of Time-Dependent Extended Sources
entries.abstract: Gravitational microlensing probes unresolved quasar accretion disc structure and compact objects in lens galaxies and is an important systematic in strong-lens time-delay cosmography. Most analyses use static microlensing map simulations because evolving individual microlenses and caustics is computationally prohibitive. We present Microcaustics, a GPU-accelerated Python package built on PyTorch for dynamical microlensing of time-dependent extended sources in strong gravitational lenses. It combines a local-exact/far-field deflection solver, source-directed lens-plane scouting with temporal reuse, and biquadratic inverse polygon mapping (IPM). GPU batching and fused Triton rasterization accelerate the calculation, while binary caustic labels track source-centred crossings. Across three simulated quadruply lensed quasar systems, our package generates a 10-year, 147-frame multiband light curve in an amortized median of 0.68 s (0.88 s with labels) on a consumer GPU with a median light-curve RMSE of 0.35 mmag, while recovering every reference source-centred caustic crossing. At comparable map accuracy, the batched throughput is 780 times higher than that of a recent CUDA IPM implementation and extrapolates to a speedup of millions relative to classic GPU-D. We demonstrate that our IPM converges as $N_{\rm ray}^{-0.84}$, approaching the idealized $N_{\rm ray}^{-1}$ convergence rate of piecewise-affine IPM and improving upon the $N_{\rm ray}^{-1/2}$ inverse ray-shooting rate. We also introduce a GPU-resident general relativistic and reverberating quasar source model and demonstrate our method with an evolving supernova source. These advances make fully dynamical stellar fields practical for Bayesian and simulation-based inference.

entries.title: Evidence for Suppressed Non-thermal Broadening in a Flare Ribbon from Stereoscopic Observations
entries.abstract: Flare ribbons mark the footpoints of newly reconnected magnetic loops and are commonly associated with strong plasma flows and enhanced non-thermal broadening of transition-region lines due to impulsive energy deposition. However, the mechanisms governing energy transport into flare ribbons remain uncertain, particularly under different magnetic field configurations. We investigate the energy deposition process at a flare ribbon near a sunspot by determining the physical nature of its small-scale downflows. We study small-scale downflows in a remote ribbon during the M7.7-class event on 30 September 2024, using coordinated observations from SDO, IRIS, and Solar Orbiter. We use stereoscopic imaging from Solar Orbiter and IRIS to detect plane-of-sky motions on small scales (200 km). We conduct spectroscopic analysis of IRIS Si IV profiles, complemented by C II and Mg II diagnostics. Apparent downflow speeds measured from Solar Orbiter imaging (limb view) are 85-130 km/s, while IRIS images (disk view) reveal plane-of-sky speeds of 70-85 km/s. In contrast, IRIS Si IV profiles at the brightest ribbon pixels are well approximated by a single Gaussian, with minimal Doppler shifts and unexpectedly small non-thermal widths (10 km/s). Peak Si IV emission also coincides with a deeper Mg II central reversal, while electron densities are one to two orders of magnitude higher than typical quiet-Sun values. The absence of significant line-of-sight velocities and non-thermal broadening differs from typical flare-ribbon behavior. Our results are consistent with a scenario in which plasma motions are guided by highly inclined (nearly horizontal) magnetic fields in chromospheric canopy and are not accompanied by strong turbulence or wave motions. This study suggests that flare ribbons can exhibit a wide diversity of lower-atmospheric responses and emphasizes the critical role of magnetic field geometry.

entries.title: High-Frequency Transverse Waves in Chromospheric Fibrils Revealed by DKIST
entries.abstract: Chromospheric fibrils are ubiquitous dynamical structures that can support magnetohydrodynamic waves and may contribute to energy transport in the solar atmosphere. Using high-resolution observations from the Visible Broadband Imager (VBI) onboard the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST), we investigate transverse oscillations of H$α$ fibrils. Our observations encompass both quiet-Sun and active regions. The results reveal that high-frequency transverse oscillations are highly prevalent in fibrils across different magnetic environments. The detected oscillations exhibit typical periods of 56 $\pm$ 49 s, displacement amplitudes of 37 $\pm$ 25 km, velocity amplitudes of 6 $\pm$ 4 km\,s$^{-1}$, and phase velocities of 21 $\pm$ 13 km\,s$^{-1}$. Under typical chromospheric conditions, the estimated wave energy flux ranges from 20 to 200 W\,m$^{-2}$. The characteristics of these transverse oscillations are consistent with those of Alfvénic kink-mode waves. Our results reveal the existence of the high-frequency, small-amplitude transverse waves in chromospheric fibrils and providing new constraints on their contribution to the chromospheric and coronal heating.

entries.title: Identifying Planetary Nebulae Candidates from IPHAS and VPHAS+ Surveys via YOLO Deep Learning Models
entries.abstract: We present a deep learning detection method capable of effectively identifying planetary nebulae (PNe) on IPHAS and VPHAS+ surveys. Our detection pipeline is based on the YOLO architecture and is adaptable to other datasets. Using the HiPS system, we preprocess and augment the $r$, $i$, and $Hα$ bands to produce two red, green, and blue (RGB) image datasets: (1) $640 \times 640$ px images at full resolution, and (2) $1 280 \times 1 280$ px images designed to capture extended objects up to $0.2$ deg. Images of $\sim 2600$ PNe are labelled using the HASH database. The loss function and evaluation metrics are adapted to the diffuse and low-contrast nature of PNe; a very low intersection over union (IoU) threshold ($1\%$) is used. A $k$-fold cross validation shows that the YOLOv12m model achieves an average precision of $0.979$ on the first dataset. At a confidence threshold of $0.15$, it achieves a precision rate of $98.7\%$ and a recall rate of $97.4\%$. We deployed our system (on $1280 \times 1280$ images) on the full surveys' coverage ($\sim 3755$ deg$^2$), and present a preliminary analysis of the detection results. The system is robust against artifacts such as CCD corner defects and HiPS tile joints. Our convolutional-neural-network-based model achieved excellent results on the test set, comparable to-or exceeding-that of a recent Swin Transformer approach. However, a challenge persists when applying deep learning models to extensive and densely populated Galactic fields: the development of an automated system that can effectively discriminate PNe from mimics that human experts are able to distinguish (e.g., H II regions). We outline possible improvements for future work.

entries.title: Large dust grains escaping from a supernova remnant
entries.abstract: Dust grains produced in the supernova (SN) ejecta at early ages are partially destroyed in hot gas of the SN remnant. Large grains owing to their inertia can overtake the forward shock front of the remnant and move through the ambient interstellar medium. Using one-dimensional gas dynamics including the dust destruction we study the transport of dust grains inside the SN remnant and the ambient medium. Here we estimate the surviving and escaping mass fractions depending on the cut-off (maximum) size in a power-law distribution of grain sizes. We found that these fractions follow closely each other at late age of the SN remnant, i.e. almost all grains, which have survived in the remnant, leave it for the ambient interstellar medium. At the age of 30 kyr -- the onset of the radiative phase with density $n\sim 1$ cm$^{-3}$ with solar metallicity -- the escaping/surviving mass fractions for the cut-off size of several microns reach about $0.7-0.8$. The major part of these grains have size larger than $1~μ$m and initially located at distances $\gtrsim 0.2$ of the ejecta core radius. Later dust grains at velocity of several hundreds km/s escaping the remnant continue to be destroyed due to kinetic sputtering in the interstellar medium. Grains with sizes of several microns are destroyed marginally and therefore will survive in the interstellar gas. After decelerating of grains in the medium the surviving mass fraction of grains produced in the SN remnant, which evolves in an ambient gas with $n$ from 1 to 100 cm$^{-3}$, is from $\sim 0.5$ to $\sim 0.3$, respectively, for the cut-off grain size $a_{cut} = 10~μ$m. A decrease of the cut-off size in the distribution results in lower surviving mass fraction.

entries.title: Strong gravitational lensing with Euclid
entries.abstract: Euclid data is going to lead to the discovery of approximately 10^5 new strong gravitational lenses, thereby increasing the number of known lenses by a factor of 30. Such an impressive jump has the potential to revolutionise the field of strong lensing, by covering an ever-increasing range in the parameter space occupied by the lenses and lensed sources, and by uncovering rare and precious strong lens systems. The first quick data release of Euclid has already revealed hundreds of lenses, giving us a taste of what the final Euclid strong lens sample might look like. These lenses include a variety of objects acting as deflectors, from isolated galaxies to clusters, from early-type galaxies to edge-on disks. As many as four double-source plane lenses, in which one foreground object lenses two galaxies at two different redshifts, have already been discovered. As more data are acquired, it might become possible to detect the strong lensing signature of dwarf galaxy satellites, and to find lenses with an unusually large number of images. In this paper, we try to anticipate the kind of discoveries that these data will bring along.

entries.title: A heterogeneous set of unusual quasars selected from astrometry and broad-band photometry
entries.abstract: The aim of this study is to explore methods for how to identify new quasars with different properties with regard to reddening, redshift, the presence of broad absorption lines from outflows, or other rare properties affecting the broad-band colours. We use Gaia-based astrometric pre-selection to study only sources that have zero parallax and zero proper motion within errors. We subsequently match these sources with information from wide-area photometric surveys and build colour-colour diagrams. Based on these diagrams we select targets for follow-up spectroscopy. In the subsequent analysis we also apply observations from SPHEREx to firmly establish redshifts. We secure spectroscopic observations for 24 sources. Of these, three are found to be stars and the remaining 21 are classified as quasars spanning a redshift range from z=0.139 to z=3.732. The majority of the sources located away from the normal quasar locus in colour-colour diagrams are found to be broad-absorption-line quasars. A single source, the lowest redshift source at z=0.139, is reminiscent of the so-called Little Red Dots found at high redshifts with JWST. Using the simple procedure followed here it is possible to locate previously undiscovered quasars with interesting properties, in particular Broad Absorption Line quasars and quasars with unusual extinction.

entries.title: specwizard: A Public Python Framework for Creating Synthetic Absorption Spectra from Hydrodynamical Simulations
entries.abstract: We present specwizard, a publicly available modular Python package for generating synthetic absorption spectra from hydrodynamical simulations. The code combines atomic data from the National Institute of Standards and Technology database with ionisation fractions computed using the cloudy spectral synthesis code for multiple ionising backgrounds, enabling consistent modelling of bound--bound and bound--free absorption for resonant transitions of all ions. specwizard employs a column-density--conserving projection scheme, includes natural line broadening for the Lyman series, and offers optional treatments of instrumental resolution and noise for direct comparison with high-resolution quasar spectra. As example applications of the code, we shoot sightlines through the eagle cosmological simulation to generate a z = 3.2 synthetic quasar spectrum containing H i Lyman-series transitions, including damping wings and Lyman-limit absorption. Additionally, we compute metal-absorption lines probing the circumgalactic medium of simulated galaxies, and investigate the correlated absorption of H i and Si iii. We demonstrate that specwizard applied to outputs from eagle accurately reproduces key observational diagnostics of the Lyman-alpha forest, including the redshift evolution of the mean transmission, the transmission PDF and the transmission power spectrum. We take advantage of the fact that the eagle simulation also reproduces the measured evolution of the temperature-density relation to infer the evolution of the amplitude of the ionizing background, finding excellent agreement with recent theoretical models and measurements.

entries.title: Probing Planet Formation within 10 au: Dust Substructures in Extremely Compact Protoplanetary Disks
entries.abstract: ALMA high-resolution surveys have so far focused mainly on large, bright protoplanetary disks, where substructures are routinely detected, leaving compact disks poorly characterized. Yet, the survival of millimeter emission in Class II sources implies that radial drift must have been halted by pressure traps, previously undetected due to limited angular resolution. We present ALMA Band 7 (0.9 mm) continuum observations of 11 of the smallest ($R_{68} < 10$ au) Class II disks in Lupus, reaching $0.02''$ (2 au) resolution, the highest currently available with ALMA at this wavelength. We detect substructures in 4 disks, including a clear inner cavity of radius 1.6 au, and hints of substructure in 3 more. Two disks also host faint outer rings beyond their bright inner core. Combining these results with demographic information on Class II disks observed with ALMA, we examine how the substructure detection rate varies with disk size, restricting to disks whose diameter is resolved by at least 3 resolution elements. We find that nearly all disks ($\gtrsim$95%) larger than 30 au show substructures, compared to a still substantial $\sim$50% between 3 and 30 au, with the lower rate likely affected by optical depth. The planet masses required to open gaps within 5 au fall in the super-Earth to mini-Neptune regime. These results demonstrate that substructures are ubiquitous across the disk population, and that planet formation conditions can be probed down to a few au from the host star.

entries.title: Rotochemical heating of neutron stars in 2D
entries.abstract: The matter inside a spinning-down neutron star (NS) undergoes a slow compression that may drive it out of chemical equilibrium and, consequently, trigger non-equilibrium nuclear reactions that can heat up the star. This phenomenon is called rotochemical heating, and it is relatively well-investigated in the literature. Historically, it has been studied almost exclusively via 1D spherically symmetric models. However, rapidly rotating NSs are not spherically symmetric. We present pioneering simulations of rotochemical heating in full General Relativity in 2D axially symmetric models without relying on the slow rotation approximation. We explicitly follow thermal, mechanical, and chemical evolution of rotating NSs as they spin down taking into account both radial and angular distributions of temperature, composition, and mechanical structure. The simplest model is employed: only nucleonic composition, only the non-equilibrium modified Urca process as the main heating/cooling mechanism, and no superfluidity. We analyze the impact of the magnetic field strength as well as the effects of the heat blanketing envelope, initial rotation frequency, NS mass, and core EOS. Most of our conclusions coincide with the results of previous works on this topic, with one important exception. We have found a strong dependence of the cooling curves during the rotochemical heating phases on the core EOS, whereas in the literature it was regarded as very weak. The most likely explanation for this discrepancy is that the authors of the previous works have not considered EOSs with wide enough range of variation of the symmetry energy as a function of density.

entries.title: The contact frontier in Galactic civilization networks: radial structure and the Galactic habitable zone
entries.abstract: The probability of interstellar contact depends not only on the abundance of technological civilizations but also on their spatial connectivity. Treating civilizations as nodes linked whenever their separation is smaller than the distance a signal travels within a communicative lifetime, we determine the radial structure of Galactic civilization networks. An exponential stellar disc replaces the uniform disc of earlier work, and the fraction of stars hosting civilizations may vary with radius as a Galactic Habitable Zone (GHZ). The isolation, contact and network transitions are frontiers several kiloparsecs wide, not boundaries: the contact frontier is set entirely by the disc scale length, and the network frontier, broadened by gradient percolation, stays near 1.5 scale lengths. The two frontiers overlap over a band containing the Sun, where both transitions proceed at once. Within this factorized GHZ model, the radius of peak civilization density depends only logarithmically on the strength of supernova sterilization, and the wide range of published peak radii, from the Galactic centre to 12 kpc, is reproduced primarily by varying that one parameter. Under the present normalization, the location of the zone has only a modest effect on the local contact probability, whereas the modelled Galactic connectivity is minimized when the civilization-density peak lies near the solar Galactocentric radius, where current determinations place the peak.

entries.title: LHAASO Constraints on New-Source Cosmic Rays:Abundance Scenarios and Injection Spectral Indices
entries.abstract: Recent LHAASO observations indicate that microquasars and massive star clusters contribute to Galactic cosmic rays, and likely also to the pre-knee spectral hardening. Their markedly different astrophysical environments, compared with supernova remnants (SNRs), may imprint distinct cosmic-ray abundances. We investigate the spectra and composition of new-source cosmic rays under two abundance scenarios: Case-1, the SNR-like composition with enhanced heavy nuclei, and Case-2, the surface abundances of microquasar companion stars. We constrain injection spectral indices using LHAASO proton, helium, and all-particle spectra, and use their <lnA> data for model discrimination. Under the assumption of a unified heavy-element injection spectrum, Case-2 fits the <lnA> data significantly better than Case-1, but at the cost of large, physically unmotivated differences between heavy-element and He injection indices. This suggests the need to either relax the unified heavy-element injection-index assumption or explore alternative abundance patterns. We predict that if the new-source composition follows Case-1, the individual elemental spectral indices before the knee should remain nearly consistent; if it follows Case-2, the Mg, Si, and Fe spectra will be significantly softer than those of He, C, and O. Future element-resolved energy-spectrum measurements by HERD and LHAASO will provide a decisive test of this discriminating feature.

entries.title: A Parsec-Scale Transient High-Frequency-Peaked Radio Source in the Very Large Array Sky Survey Brightening and Fading over a Decadal Timescale
entries.abstract: A subset of active galactic nuclei (AGN) manifests as compact radio sources with peaked radio spectra, commonly referred to as peaked-spectrum (PS) sources. Generally, PS sources are interpreted as young radio jets, but the early evolution of the jet is rarely observed and not fully understood. Here, we present VT J182357-234511 (VT J1823-2345), a radio transient in the Very Large Array Sky Survey (VLASS) that resembles a PS source. Notable properties of VT J1823-2345 include: (i) brightening by a factor of 3 between 1996 and 2021 at 1.4 GHz, (ii) peaked spectra with high frequency peaks at $ν_{\mathrm{p,obs}}\gtrsim6\,\mathrm{GHz}$, (iii) a peaked 3 GHz light curve that has been fading since 2023, (iv) a resolved Gaussian (major-axis) size of 0.4 mas in 2024, and (v) a linear polarization fraction $p_{\mathrm{L}}\simeq0.73\%$ at 8.8 GHz with an extreme Faraday rotation measure $\mathrm{RM_{\mathrm{obs}}} \sim +12,000\,\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{m}^{-2}$. On the sky, VT J1823-2345 coincides with a supernova remnant and an F-type star, but no background galaxy is seen. Based on the multi-wavelength properties, we disfavor Galactic transients, explosive extragalactic transients, and blazar variability as plausible explanations. We argue that VT J1823-2345 is consistent with a "short-lived" parsec-scale PS source with a decades-old jet that does not grow into a large-scale radio galaxy. From comparing the full VLASS light curves, we speculate that VT J1823-2345 is similar to many VLASS nuclear transients reported in the literature, which may represent an emerging class of transient radio jets, perhaps related to episodic AGN activity or jetted tidal disruption events.

entries.title: A Step-Like Transition Underlying the Life and Death of Galaxies
entries.abstract: How galaxies stop forming stars is a complex and central problem in astrophysics. Numerous physical mechanisms have been proposed, yet a simple, unified framework connecting these mechanisms remains lacking. Here, we derive a step-function quenching response from the fundamental principle of gas mass conservation, governed by the competition between gas-supply and gas-depletion timescales. This response also enables the gas-supply timescale to be inferred from the observed quenched fraction. Applying this method to approximately 350,000 galaxies, we find a characteristic gas-supply timescale of ~1 Gyr, reveal distinct inside-out and outside-in quenching signatures associated with supermassive black holes and dark matter halos, respectively, and identify galaxies with intermediate stellar surface mass densities as occupying a critical state for quenching and rejuvenation. Our work establishes a unified physical framework in which a simple step-function response captures how diverse physical processes regulate galaxy quenching and the resumption of star formation through their effects on the competition between gas-supply and gas-depletion timescales.

entries.title: Modelling the 6.7 GHz Methanol Flaring in G358.93-0.03 Using the Maxwell-Bloch Framework
entries.abstract: We model selected 6.7 GHz methanol flare profiles in G358.93-0.03 using the one-dimensional Maxwell-Bloch framework. The 2019 non-periodic flare, associated with an accretion burst, produced complex single-dish light curves characterized by sharp rises, multiple peaks, secondary structure, and extended decays. For six representative velocity channels, we model each light curve as a sum of scaled intensity responses from effective emitting systems driven by phenomenological pump pulses of fixed width but with component-dependent background rates, amplitudes, and arrival times. The inferred initial inverted column densities correspond to characteristic superradiance timescales $T_{R,0} \simeq 0.3$-$1.4~{\rm d}$, which are shorter than the adopted dephasing and relaxation timescales, $T_2 = 6.9~{\rm d}$ and $T_1 = 144.4~{\rm d}$. The fitted components therefore lie in the fast-transient superradiance regime. Existent VLBI observations motivate the possibility that a single-dish velocity channel blends emission from multiple unresolved flaring regions, although these observations are not used as direct fitting constraints. Although the decomposition is not unique, it provides a physically motivated description of the complex flare morphology within a unified Maxwell-Bloch framework.

entries.title: Can bosenovae deplete the galactic dark matter?
entries.abstract: No: neither through the bosenovae of gravitational atoms formed around stars and compact objects, nor through those of boson stars formed in the galactic dark-matter halo. We assume that all the dark matter consists of ultralight bosons with attractive self-interactions, which can be captured in the gravitational potential of astrophysical objects or condense into self-gravitating configurations. When these systems collapse in a bosenova, part of their mass is turned into relativistic radiation that escapes the galaxy. We bound the mass that a single object can eject and sum it over realistic models of the Milky Way and of other types of galaxies. For gravitational atoms, with realistic stellar populations and stellar evolution, the stars of the Milky Way deplete at most $ε^{\rm GA}_\star\simeq3\times10^{-9}$ of its halo, and the pump is equally negligible in other galaxies. The central black hole, Sgr A$^*$, could reach $ε^{\rm GA}\sim10^{-3}$, but only for a boson mass disfavoured by ultrafaint dwarf galaxies and beyond the validity of the perturbative treatment, where only a geometric bound on the dark matter flux is available. For boson stars feeding on the rest of the halo, these would radiate at most $\sim3\times10^{-5}$ of the Milky-Way halo and $0.1\%$ of a DF2-like one.

entries.title: Dynamics of a switchback-like magnetic deflection induced by a propagating coronal jet
entries.abstract: Parker Solar Probe (PSP) revealed the ubiquity of switchbacks (SBs), sharp, localised magnetic deflections in the nascent solar wind, renewing interest in their origin. One proposed mechanism involves solar jets: collimated, impulsive features driven by magnetic reconnection that launch Alfvénic torsional wavefronts into the heliosphere. We test whether realistic spacecraft sampling of a propagating solar jet produces in-situ signatures consistent with PSP observations. We also examine the 3D magnetic topology of the resulting structures and how deflection amplitudes evolve with the ambient plasma environment. We perform a 3D magnetohydrodynamic simulation of a solar jet in the ambient solar wind, embedding a virtual spacecraft trajectory based on PSP's actual 22nd-perihelion orbit to generate synthetic measurements. The simulation reproduces SB-like signatures with durations and profiles consistent with PSP observations, confirming earlier results from simplified trajectories. We visualise the fully 3D magnetic topology of a jet-driven SB region, identifying two field-line families: one with a single deflection and another with two sequential deflections along the same field line. Both are outward-propagating Alfvénic structures. Deflection amplitudes depend strongly on background plasma $β$, increasing substantially in low-$β$ regions and evolving more moderately where $β\sim 1$. These results show that solar jets can produce Alfvénic, SB-like structures along realistic spacecraft trajectories. Their topology is inherently 3D and structurally diverse, and their evolution depends on ambient plasma $β$. Complete magnetic reversals would require longer residence times in low-$β$ environments. Our findings support a solar origin for a fraction of SBs and constrain interpretations of their underlying magnetic structure.

entries.title: Binary-lens amplification of starlight: from magnification flares to quasi-periodic tracking of orbital evolution
entries.abstract: Supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHB) are expected at the center of galaxies as a result of galaxy mergers. The dynamics and evolution of SMBHBs shed light on the evolution and formation of galaxies, the gravitational wave background and the nature of gravity. Many methods have been proposed to identify sub-parsec SMBHBs via the detection of gravitational waves or the modulation of the emission from the surrounding gaseous environment. In a previous study, we proposed a new method of identifying SMBHBs in non-active galactic nuclei via gravitational lensing. The caustics, i.e. the source positions with a divergent magnification, exhibit a complex extended geometry which rotates with the binary period. Each caustic-crossing produces an extreme magnification by up to a factor of $10^{6}$. In this work, we generalize the previous study and describe the rich phenomenology of binary-lens amplification of starlight (BLAST). We explore the electromagnetic transients produced when accounting for the relative proper motion of the source, either a single or a binary star, the eccentricity and precession of the SMBHB, and the relative inclination. Systems where a star rapidly drifts across the caustic produce a single- or double-peaked flare. In the opposite limit, a star with no relative proper motion produces quasi-periodic lensed starlight (QPLS), i.e., repeated peaks that track the system's orbital evolution. We determine the expected magnification and peak duration in different circumstances, and calculate the magnification curves and their Fourier transforms. This study may help construct search pipelines to identify SMBHBs in electromagnetic time-domain surveys.

entries.title: GRB 181201A: Spectropolarimetric Constraints on Prompt Emission and Magnetic Field Structure
entries.abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) have served as testbeds for high-energy astrophysical phenomena since their discovery over 50 years ago. GRB detections reveal diverse properties across events, complicating efforts to constrain their emission mechanisms, magnetic fields, jet structures, and compositions. Spectropolarimetry is a powerful tool utilized to disentangle these properties. INTEGRAL/IBIS has previously detected three polarized GRBs 041219A ($65\pm 26$%), 061122 ($>$33%) and 140206A ($>$28%). We present the time-integrated and time-resolved analyses of the fourth-polarized GRB 181201A. This GRB exhibits high polarization ($81.5^{+17.2}_{-15.7}$%) over three time bins with the highest signal-to-noise ratio, and the polarization angle (PA) shows a modest temporal evolution. The photon index does not cross the synchrotron line-of-death and shows a hard-to-soft evolution. A high degree of polarization (PD) tends to disfavor a photospheric emission model, as previous studies indicate that this model yields PD $<$ 20%. A modest evolution in the PA points towards a non-axisymmetric jet with a multi-patch emission. Our results indicate that under standard synchrotron conditions, the magnetic field is coherent but lacks global structure. Moreover, the field has multiple patches, but only one or a few dominate due to high degrees of polarization, which overlap with the intrinsic maximum of synchrotron emission within 3$σ$ errors. The high PD is also indicative of the Compton Drag scenario, but only under certain conditions, such as viewing the relativistic jet near its edge. However, given our error bars and the scope for improvement in our pipeline, we cannot strongly favor either scenario; both may remain viable.

entries.title: Transient PULSE: Code for the Transient Propagation of UltraLight (pseudo)Scalars to Earth
entries.abstract: We present Transient PULSE, a software package that numerically implements a previously developed source-to-detector framework for transient ultralight bosonic signals from astrophysical bursts. Predicting these signals relies on connecting the source emission spectrum to its evolution during propagation and the resulting observables at a terrestrial detector. The package discretizes a user supplied energy spectrum into momentum modes, propagates them through a specified matter density profile and constructs the time-frequency energy density distribution at Earth, accounting for dispersion and in-medium screening effects. This treatment accommodates non-Gaussian source spectra and provides inputs for detector specific analyses. A complementary analytical module estimates coupling sensitivities, arrival time delays and screening thresholds from parameterized source and detector properties.
